areas.title: Bake pipeline (bake_all.py, bake_camp_lightmap.py, bake_ground.py, export_casters.cjs)
areas.summary: The bake pipeline is four steps driven by props/bake_all.py (83 lines): (1) layout: starts python http.server on :8765, node props/shadow/export_casters.cjs drives headless Chromium (SwiftShader) through the whole camp page and writes props/shadow/layout_picked.json (plus a casters_*.glb nothing reads); (2) light: Blender runs props/camp/bake_camp_lightmap.py, which exec()s the three lived builders (each does a factory reset, rebuilds, re-renders 7 textures incl. 3 Cycles CPU renders of the wood stack, and overwrites props/lived/*.glb), factory-resets again, builds the picked set (13 objects, 9 discarded), re-imports the lived GLBs, unwraps one shared atlas, then makes 16 bpy.ops.object.bake calls at 512 samples with adaptive sampling off (11 at 4096: AO, sun, sun-open, 4 light groups + 4 back-face passes for two thin cards; 5 ground passes at 1024), writes camp_lm_{4k,2k,1k}.png and camp_lm_sun_* (2k/1k are box-downsampled from the 4k, not re-baked), two ground PNGs, camp_lights.json, four GLBs and their base64 .txt; (3) ktx: toktx re-encodes five PNGs to .ktx2.txt and flips a flag in camp_lights.json; (4) ground: props/ground/bake_ground.py (numpy/PIL) writes the soil JPG and mask. Nothing is stamped or hashed: every run redoes everything in its step, and nobody can tell from the repo whether committed bakes match the committed generators (the jeep GLB and the bake script both changed after the last light bake). Main themes: (a) two real bugs feeding the bake (a comment that swallowed the dead trunk's layout entry and its seating on the terrain; the fallen log's yaw mirrored in the bake); (b) layout is mirrored by hand in Python (about 25 constants) although a generated JSON already exists and camp_lights.json shows the single-source pattern working; (c) coupling by exec + monkey-patching + a GLB disk round trip instead of function calls, with outputs written in place so a failed or --unwrap-only run leaves committed files half-updated; (d) silent fallbacks in the exporter and both bakes that turn a broken page into a quietly degraded bake; (e) dead leftovers of the removed ground-shadow bake and jeep light channels; (f) GPU time: the sample budget is set for a 4k map that is not published, one pass is shadowless and deterministic yet takes 512 samples, each bake call runs one Cycles session per object (about 195 sessions), 11 float 4k images (about 3 GB) are never freed, and the 4k PNGs (35 MB per rebake, 158 MB of the 317 MB pack) are committed although the page cannot load them when published. None of the three open PRs touch any file in this area.

findings.title: A trailing comment swallowed the dead trunk's layout entry, its seating on the terrain and its triangle count

locations.snippet: blockers.push(Object.assign([c.clone(), 0.45], { wild: true }));   // wild: no worn dirt or path to it (ground.js) layout.push({ name: "DeadTrunk", x: c.x, z: c.z, y: lift(from, c), H }); count("deadTrunk", from);
"deadwood":[{"name":"FallenLog",...},{"name":"Stump",...}]  (no DeadTrunk)
elif d["name"] == "DeadTrunk":

findings.evidence: git show fac63a0 shows the line before (three statements) and after (comment inserted mid-line, so layout.push, lift() and count() are now comment text). layout_picked.json at bad3556 and 3f81d00 lists FallenLog, Stump, DeadTrunk; at b5eaa58 (current) only FallenLog and Stump. lift() (line 74) is what moves the trunk's parts to groundHeight - 0.03, so it no longer runs for the trunk. Not touched by PRs 14, 15, 16.
findings.why: Three effects: the 4.6 m dead trunk and its fungus are not seated on the terrain at the clearing rim; window.__deadwood.tris has no deadTrunk entry (triangle report rule); and the next light bake will silently lose the trunk's shadow (the committed maps from bad3556 still have it, so a rebake would be a visible regression nobody asked for).
findings.fix: Put the comment at the end of the line: blockers.push(...); layout.push({ name: "DeadTrunk", ... }); count("deadTrunk", from);   // wild: ... Then re-run the layout step so the JSON lists three pieces again.

findings.title: The fallen log's shadow caster is yawed the wrong way in the bake (about 31 degrees off the visible log)

locations.snippet: o.rotation_mode = "YXZ"; o.rotation_euler = (0, math.pi / 2, d["yaw"])   # lie along x, then yaw
yaw = Math.atan2(c.z, c.x) + Math.PI / 2 + R(-0.3, 0.3) ... .rotateY(-yaw) ... ax = V(Math.cos(yaw), 0, Math.sin(yaw))

findings.evidence: On the page the log lies along (cos yaw, sin yaw) in (x, z) because the geometry is rotated by rotateY(-yaw). The bake maps a page point to Blender (x, -z, y), so that direction is (cos yaw, -sin yaw, 0) = a Z rotation of -yaw. The script applies +yaw. With the exported yaw 1.8402 the two lines differ by (2*yaw mod pi) = 30.9 degrees (computed from layout_picked.json). The docstring rule 'yaw about up is the same angle in both' holds for three.js rotation.y values, but this layout field is a math angle applied as rotateY(-yaw). Also the caster's centre is at y + r (line 245) while the page puts it at y + 0.75 r (deadwood.js:81), and the rotation= argument on line 245 is overwritten on the next line. bad3556 changed the mode from ZYX to YXZ, so the committed maps were baked with this mirrored yaw.
findings.why: The baked ground shadow of a 2.6 m log is rotated about its middle relative to the log you see; the ends are off by about 0.67 m.
findings.fix: Use -d["yaw"] (or export the log's three.js rotation.y as rotY so the docstring rule holds everywhere), centre at d.get("y", 0) + 0.75 * d["r"], and drop the dead rotation= argument.

findings.title: The bake script never sets or prints the Cycles device; four factory resets run after the GPU wrapper

locations.snippet: sc.render.engine = "CYCLES"; sc.cycles.samples = a.samples; sc.cycles.use_adaptive_sampling = False
build_camp.reset()
bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
cmd += [GPU_RUN, "--", script, "--", *args] if GPU_RUN else [script, "--", *args]
argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]

findings.evidence: git grep for cycles.device / compute_device / OPTIX / denois in the repo: the only hits are sc.cycles.device = "CPU" in build_camp.py:739 and build_lived.py:180. gpu_run.py lives outside the repo (render-jobs on the desktop), so its contract cannot be read here. read_factory_settings resets the scene and the preferences (where the Cycles compute device type lives); it runs in build_lived.build, build_fire.build, build_laundry.build and at line 125, all after gpu_run.py started. Denoising is likewise never set. The argv split on the first "--" would hand argparse the script path unless gpu_run.py rewrites sys.argv, so that contract is also implicit.
findings.why: The single setting that decides whether a full bake takes minutes or hours lives in an unversioned wrapper, and the script would run on the CPU without saying so (also when run by the command in its own docstring). Two rebake commits 26 minutes apart suggest the GPU is in use today, but nothing in the repo guarantees or logs it.
findings.fix: After the last reset, print scene.cycles.device, the preferences' compute_device_type, the enabled devices and use_denoising; add --device (default from an env var) that sets them explicitly and aborts if a GPU was asked for and none is enabled. Document the argv contract with gpu_run.py in the docstring.
findings.estimate_or_measured: Not measured. Estimate: on CPU the 7 full-atlas 4k passes at 512 samples would take on the order of an hour or more instead of minutes.

findings.title: Outputs are written in place: a failed or --unwrap-only run leaves committed GLBs and maps out of step

locations.snippet: exec(compile(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), path, "exec"), g); call(g)
path = os.path.join(HERE, "lived.glb") ... bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=path, ...
if a.unwrap_only: sys.exit(0)
save(..., "camp_lm") ... json.dump(...camp_lights.json) ... export(picked, ...)
x, z, yaw = table[key]

findings.evidence: Step 1 overwrites props/lived/{lived,fire,laundry}.glb (committed files the .txt copies are made from) with flat-colour versions that have no light-map UVs and an unsplit SeatTop; the final versions are only written at lines 436-439. --unwrap-only exits at 218 after that overwrite. Anything raising between 83 and 435 (a KeyError at 176 for an object missing from PLACE, StopIteration at 238, a Cycles or disk error) leaves those GLBs broken, and a failure after line 405 leaves new light-map PNGs (new atlas) next to old GLB/.txt (old UVs). camp_lights.json is rewritten at 418 without the ktx2 flag, so until the ktx step runs the page uses PNGs; KTX-capable and PNG browsers can therefore see different states after a partial run.
findings.why: A full bake is costly and its outputs are committed; a crash can leave the working tree in a state that looks plausible in git status but shows scrambled light on the page.
findings.fix: Have the lived builders write to a temp dir passed in (not next to the sources); write every final output into one staging folder and os.replace() them into models/ and props/ only after the last export succeeded; make --unwrap-only write nothing outside the staging folder.

findings.title: Layout step: fixed port 8765 shared with npm run serve, server failure is silent, wait loop has no failure branch

locations.snippet: srv = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-m", "http.server", "8765", "--bind", "127.0.0.1"], cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
await p.goto(`http://localhost:8765/apps/canopy-prototype/camp.html?props=${props}&jeep=${jeep}&lm=off`);
"serve": "npx http-server -p 8765 -c-1 ."

findings.evidence: git grep 8765: package.json serve, apps/playtime-tools/shot.cjs, stickers/renderer/stk_run.cjs and stk_anim.cjs all use the same port. If something already listens there (a dev server, possibly from another checkout or worktree), Popen's bind error goes to DEVNULL, the urlopen poll succeeds against the other server and the layout is exported from whatever tree that server serves. If nothing answers within 50 x 0.2 s the loop simply ends and node is started anyway. srv.terminate() has no wait().
findings.why: The layout JSON drives both the ground bake and the deadwood shadows; exporting it from a stale tree gives a wrong bake with no error.
findings.fix: Bind port 0 (or pick a free port), pass the base URL to export_casters.cjs as an argument or env var, fail if srv.poll() is not None or the poll loop runs out, keep the server's stderr, and wait() after terminate().

findings.title: Silent fallbacks turn a broken page into a quietly degraded bake

locations.snippet: p.on("pageerror", (e) => console.log("PAGEERR", e.message));
glade: (window.__glade?.path || []) ... deadwood: window.__deadwood?.layout || [], height: window.__terrainGrid?.(128) || null
for d in (_json.load(open(_lay)).get("deadwood", []) if os.path.exists(_lay) else []):
HM = L.get("hammock") ... if L.get("entry"): ... if L.get("glade"): ... if L.get("tent"): ... if L.get("track"):

findings.evidence: Every optional read falls back to an empty value and each consumer guards with .get(), so a missing global, a page error or a missing JSON only removes features from the bake. It has already happened twice: layout_picked.json at 8ef1a2b has "deadwood": [] and the current one lost DeadTrunk (genbake-01); neither was noticed. The exporter exits 0 after page errors.
findings.why: Bakes are expensive and committed; a degraded input should stop the run, not produce a subtly different ground or light map.
findings.fix: In the exporter: collect page errors and exit 1 if any; validate the layout before writing (required keys, at least N spots, the three deadwood names, track and glade non-empty) and exit 1 with a message. In the Python consumers: read required keys with L["..."] and fail on a missing file.

findings.title: ktx runs before ground and aborts the run when toktx is missing; no preflight of tools

locations.snippet: steps = a.only or ["layout", "light", "ktx", "ground"]
TOKTX = os.environ.get("TOKTX", "toktx") ... run([TOKTX, "--t2", ...])

findings.evidence: The KTX commits are made in the cloud, not by the GPU thread (057b3ba and bc9f846: 'cloud toktx, Adriaen: cloud for now'), and the bake commits 8ef1a2b and bad3556 contain PNGs and a camp_lights.json without ktx2 but no .ktx2.txt changes. So on the desktop the default step list raises FileNotFoundError at ktx, after the long light step and before ground. Between a bake commit and the cloud KTX commit the page serves the PNG fallback (about twice the download). Blender, node, playwright, Chrome, PIL inside Blender's Python (needs PYTHONPATH with --python-use-system-env, line 39 and 82) and toktx are all only discovered when their step starts.
findings.why: A missing tool is found after the expensive step, and the ground bake is skipped by an unrelated failure.
findings.fix: Order the steps layout, ground, light, ktx (ground only needs the layout); add a preflight that resolves every tool the chosen steps need before anything runs; when toktx is absent, warn and leave ktx2 unset instead of raising. Also move the three imports inside the ktx block (66, 75, 79) to the top and close the two json file handles on line 80.

findings.title: camp-probe: shader names never match (double-escaped regex), an unused variable, server open on all interfaces

locations.snippet: (src.match(/#define SHADER_NAME (\\S+)/) || [])[1] || '?'
const fur = o.userData && o.userData.shell;
const f = path.join(ROOT, decodeURIComponent(q.url.split('?')[0])); ... }).listen(8799);

findings.evidence: Line 19 is a real function (serialised by addInitScript), so the regex literal with two backslashes matches a literal backslash followed by S characters, never a shader name: every programNames entry is '?:<hash>'. fur is assigned and never read (grep in the file). The server listens on every interface with no host argument and joins the raw URL path onto ROOT, so a raw request with ../ can read outside the repo; port 8799 is fixed with no EADDRINUSE handling.
findings.why: The probe is the tool the earlier audit's numbers came from; its program list is less useful than intended, and the server is looser than a local tool needs.
findings.fix: Use a single backslash in the regex, delete the fur line, listen(port, '127.0.0.1') and reject paths that resolve outside ROOT.

findings.why: Every placement change needs a matching edit in a 442-line Blender script that cloud threads cannot run; a miss shows up only after a GPU rebake as light in the wrong place.

(2) In the bake, assert the mirrored Python values equal that block (fails loudly on drift, output unchanged). (3) Delete the Python copies and read the block; the same file can later carry the builders' numbers for the page (soup surface, laundry line), as camp_lights.json already does for the colours.

findings.evidence: Each lived builder's build() does its own factory reset, builds, calls bake() and exports a GLB, so the only way to get its objects into the shared scene is the file on disk. All three builders also patch build_camp.densify, which flat_bake never calls. Run on their own, the builders write GLBs with baked AO and no TEXCOORD_1, which the page's lnight() materials cannot use, so the stand-alone path is no longer valid. The glTF importer does not merge vertices by default, so round-tripped meshes come back split at every hard edge and colour border; pack_islands then treats those faces as separate islands (the picked set, built in process, does not have this), which costs atlas area and adds seams.

findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate: removes 3 of 4 factory resets, 3 GLB exports and 3 imports per run (a few seconds) and may raise atlas coverage; the coverage line the script prints should be compared before and after.

locations.snippet: ap.add_argument("--margin", type=float, default=6)    # texels between islands at --size ... pack_islands(..., margin_method="ADD", margin=a.margin / a.size)

"--assign_oetf", "linear", "--assign_primaries", "none", "--genmipmap", out, f

findings.evidence: Islands are packed 6 texels apart at 4096 and each object's bake then grows an 8-pixel margin. The 26 receivers are baked one after another into the same image and Blender fills the margin for each object using only that object's own pixels as the mask, so a later object's margin can paint over the outer texels of an earlier neighbour that sits closer than 8 px. Separately, 6 texels at 4k is 1.5 texels in the 1k map phones load, the unused atlas area is black, and both paths use mipmaps (toktx --genmipmap; three.js generates them for the PNG fallback), so from the second mip level on neighbouring islands and black background mix into island edges. I have not seen the artefact; this is from the numbers.
findings.why: If it happens it shows as thin dark or bright fringes along some prop edges, strongest on phones and at a distance, and would be blamed on the bake's quality.
findings.fix: Define the gap in texels of the smallest shipped size (for example 2 texels at 1k = 8 at 4k) and derive the bake margin from it (half the gap), in one place. Baking through a joined stand-in (genbake-24) removes the per-object overwrite. Consider no mipmaps for the light maps (generateMipmaps = false with linear filtering, and no --genmipmap), which is the usual choice for atlases.

areas.title: Generators: camp props and jeep (build_camp.py, build_jeep.py)
areas.summary:
props/camp/build_camp.py (843 lines) and props/jeep/build_jeep.py (972 lines) work and are readable prop by prop, but both carry a lot that the live camp no longer uses, and they are tied to the other props scripts through monkey-patching instead of arguments. Static review only: nothing was run, so every time figure below is an estimate.

What runs today. props/bake_all.py -> bake_camp_lightmap.py imports build_camp and calls only reset(), picked(), apply_all(), BUDGET and STOVE; it swaps build_camp.bake for a flat-colour stand-in. build_camp's own AO bake, densify(), lean() and build() are reached only through the archive CLI (`build_camp.py --style ...`, which writes into props/camp/archive/). So densify() does subdivide purely for the AO bake and that inflated geometry is exported, but only for archived styles; the live GLB (camp_picked_lm.glb) is not densified, and the BUDGET decimate never triggers there. build_jeep.py is not part of bake_all at all: the jeep GLB is built by hand, its page .txt copy is made by hand, and the light bake just imports whatever GLB is on disk.

Main themes. (1) Wasted building: picked() builds the full rustic and jungle sets (12 objects) and deletes 9 of them; about three quarters of its roughly 900 Blender operator calls go to deleted parts. (2) Operator-heavy helpers: every primitive costs at least three bpy.ops calls (add, select_all, transform_apply), join() costs 2n+3, and build_jeep's outward() enters and leaves edit mode 28 times; a jeep build is about 1,100 to 1,300 operator calls and 19 EXACT booleans. In wall-clock terms this is probably seconds, not minutes; the likely big costs are the six Cycles preview stills build_jeep renders by default and the Cycles bakes. (3) Hidden coupling: build_camp.densify is overwritten in five places and build_camp.bake in one, and it only works because of import order. (4) Archived styles (storybook, rustic fire/tent/hammock/lantern, jungle except the hammock, toy, camper, the open wheel) are about 39% of build_camp.py and 13% of build_jeep.py, and the live props are built inside them (trims made for the camp have changed the archived rustic builder). (5) Triangle rule: a few concrete leftovers (a fully enclosed winch drum, lug bottoms and nut backs on five wheels, seat stump caps, tent wall columns that only existed for vertex AO). (6) Stale docstrings throughout, and constants mirrored by hand between Python and the page. None of the three open PRs touches props/, so generator-only fixes conflict with nothing.

def rustic(): ... out["Fire"] ... out["Seat"] ... out["Tent"] ... out["Hammock"] ... out["Lantern"] ... out["Table"]
def jungle(plain_posts=False):
bpy.data.objects.remove(objs["Seat"]); bpy.data.objects.remove(objs["Lantern"])

findings.evidence: Read picked(), rustic(), jungle(), wall_tent() line by line and counted parts and operator calls by hand. Kept: rustic Seat (4 parts) and Table (11), jungle Hammock (5), wall_tent (42) = 62 parts, about 218 bpy.ops calls. Built then removed: rustic Fire (21 parts), A-frame Tent (23), Hammock (8), Lantern (3; removed by bake_camp_lightmap.py:154 because camp/lanterns.js draws the lanterns), jungle Fire with tripod (27), bench (22), lean-to with 36 solidified leaves (82), Lantern (3), Table (26) = 215 parts, about 690 bpy.ops calls. Checked that none of the kept objects reads the module rng (rough_up, drop_faces, painted_bamboo, sag_sheet, wall_tent, stove_kettle use none), so skipping the discarded builders cannot change the kept geometry.
findings.why: Every light bake (the only live caller, bake_camp_lightmap.py:126) pays for building two archived prop sets it deletes a few lines later. It also means the live Seat, Table and Hammock live inside archived style builders: the camp-review trims at lines 430-454 and the plain_posts flag at 688-697 changed the archived rustic and jungle builders to serve the picked set.
findings.fix: Split rustic() and jungle() into one function per prop (rustic_seat(M), rustic_table(M), rustic_lantern(M), jungle_hammock(M, plain_posts), ...) plus rustic_mats()/jungle_mats(). rustic() and jungle() call them in today's order so the archived styles consume rng exactly as before. picked() then calls only rustic_seat, rustic_table, jungle_hammock(plain_posts=True) and wall_tent(); the rename loop at 798-800 and the removes go away. Verify with a geometry-only comparison in bpy (vertex and face arrays of Seat, Table, Hammock, Tent before and after; no Cycles needed).
findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate, not measured: about 690 of about 900 operator calls and 215 of 277 parts are wasted; at roughly 0.3 to 3 ms per call that is 0.2 to 2 s per bake run. The larger gain is clarity and removing the coupling to archived builders.

findings.title: build_camp.densify and build_camp.bake are monkey-patched from six places and only work through import order

locations.snippet: if not o.get("coarse"): densify(o, o.get("ao_edge", 0.13))
build_camp.densify = lambda o, *a, **k: apply_all(o)   # bake() calls it: no splitting, only apply transforms
build_camp.densify = lambda o, *a, **k: None
build_camp.densify = lambda o, *_: apply_all(o)
build_camp.densify = lambda o, *_: apply_all(o)
build_camp.densify = lambda o, *_: apply_all(o)
build_camp.bake = flat_bake ... exec(compile(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), path, "exec"), g)

findings.evidence: grep for densify and build_camp. across props/: five assignments to build_camp.densify (two different replacements: one applies transforms, one does nothing) and one to build_camp.bake. bake() looks up densify as a module global at call time, so the last assignment wins for every later caller in the same Blender process. The lived scripts and build_jeep do `from build_camp import bake`, which binds the function at import time, so flat_bake only reaches them because bake_camp_lightmap.py assigns it (line 80) before it execs them (line 86). Every caller except the archive CLI switches densify off, so the real densify() is default-on behaviour that nobody in the live pipeline wants.
findings.why: This is the most fragile piece of the generators. The behaviour of bake() depends on which script was imported last; reordering an import, or importing build_jeep into the bake script, silently changes results (for the jeep, the apply_all variant would bake the doors' open rotation into the meshes; the comment at line 921 says it must not). It is also why the lived GLBs make a round trip (build writes lived.glb with flat colours, the bake imports it and writes it again).
findings.fix: Make the choices arguments. bake(objs, samples, split_edge=None, apply=True): no splitting unless asked; build_camp.build() passes split_edge=0.13 for archive remakes; build_jeep passes apply=False. Give the lived build() functions a `colour=` argument (the AO bake or a flat-colour function) that bake_camp_lightmap.py passes in, and move flat_bake next to bake so both share the 'Baked' material code (build_camp.py:773-782 and bake_camp_lightmap.py:74-78 are the same block). Then delete all six assignments. Touches the lived scripts and the bake script, so coordinate with their owners.

findings.title: Each primitive costs three or more Blender operator calls; join() costs 2n+3; edit-mode toggles for normals

locations.snippet: bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(...) / primitive_uv_sphere_add / primitive_ico_sphere_add / primitive_cube_add / primitive_torus_add
def apply_all(o): bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT") ... modifier_apply ... transform_apply | def join(objs, name): for o in objs: apply_all(o)
def bevel(o, w, seg=2): apply_all(o) | def rough_up(...): apply_all(o) | def drop_faces(o, test): apply_all(o)
apply_all(lg); bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="EDIT"); bpy.ops.mesh.select_all(action="SELECT"); bpy.ops.mesh.bisect(...); bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")
def outward(o): select_all; mode_set(EDIT); mesh.select_all; normals_make_consistent(inside=False); mode_set(OBJECT)
def upper_half(o, z): apply_all(o); mode_set(EDIT); select_all; bisect; mode_set(OBJECT)

findings.evidence: AST count: 32 bpy.ops call sites in build_camp.py and 19 in build_jeep.py; only 12 sit lexically in loops, but the helpers are called from loops. Per part: one primitive_*_add, then join() runs apply_all on every part (select_all + one modifier_apply per modifier + transform_apply), then select_all + join + transform_apply once. So a plain part costs 3 calls, a bevelled box 6 (box() and bevel() call apply_all once more), a table leg 7 (cyl, rough_up, drop_faces, join each apply). select_all and transform_apply walk every object in the scene, so cost per call grows with the number of parts already built. Hand count: picked() about 900 calls (277 parts); expedition jeep about 1,100 to 1,300 (about 253 parts, 28 outward() calls = 140 operator calls and 56 mode switches, 19 EXACT boolean applies at lines 433-468, plus the LOD). The per-part transform_apply inside join() is redundant: object.join already moves each mesh into the active object's space and line 260 applies the joined object's transform. build_camp.stove_kettle (line 616) already uses bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals, which is what the edit-mode operator in outward() runs internally.
findings.why: This is the pattern Adriaen suspected. It is roughly quadratic in part count and it is shared by the lived scripts, which import the same helpers, so it gets worse as props are added. In absolute time it is probably a few seconds per build, far below the Cycles steps, so it is worth fixing for scale and clarity rather than as an emergency.
findings.fix: In three small steps, each checked by comparing vertex and face arrays before and after. (a) join(): select the parts once, bpy.ops.object.convert(target="MESH") to apply all modifiers in one call, then join and one transform_apply: 4 calls instead of 2n+m+3. (b) outward(): bm = bmesh.new(); bm.from_mesh(me); bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces[:]); bm.to_mesh(me): no operator, no mode switch. Same for the two bisects (bmesh.ops.bisect_plane). (c) Build primitives without operators: bmesh.ops.create_cube / create_cone / create_uvsphere / create_icosphere with matrix= the final transform (these are what the primitive operators call, so topology and vertex order stay the same), wrapped by one mesh_obj() helper. Step (c) belongs in the shared library (gencamp-17).
findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate, not measured: about 900 operator calls for picked() and 1,100 to 1,300 for the expedition jeep; likely 1 to 5 s each in background Blender. Geometry may differ in the last float bits after (a) and (c).

findings.evidence: Read preview() and build(). Unless --no-preview is passed, each build renders six views (front, back, detail, open, door, wheel) at 900x700, 48 samples; bake() set sc.cycles.device = "CPU" just before (build_camp.py:739), so they render on the CPU. The PNGs go to props/jeep/preview_<style>_<tag>.png, which .gitignore excludes (props/jeep/preview_*.png). build() returns the list of paths but the only caller (line 972) ignores it. The module docstring (lines 10 and 18) still describes one still per style and a preview_all.png that no code writes.
findings.why: Regenerating the jeep GLB after a small geometry change pays for six CPU path-traced renders nobody asked for. The previews are useful when showing a change, so they should stay available, but as an explicit choice.
findings.fix: Make previews opt-in: replace --no-preview with --preview (optionally taking the view list, which makes VIEWS and --views unnecessary), drop the unused return value, and move preview() and doors-open view setup to props/jeep/preview_jeep.py if the library split goes ahead. Update the docstring. The GLBs are unchanged.
findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate, not measured: six 900x700 renders at 48 samples on CPU are likely the largest single cost of a default jeep build (tens of seconds to a few minutes, against seconds for geometry).

findings.title: The jeep is outside bake_all: no build step, no staleness check, and its page .txt copy is made by hand

jall = import_glb(os.path.join(ROOT, "props", "jeep", f"jeep_{a.jeep}.glb"))
steps = a.only or ["layout", "light", "ktx", "ground"]

findings.evidence: git grep for b64encode and base64 across the repo (engine excluded): only bake_all.py (KTX2) and bake_camp_lightmap.py (camp_picked_lm, lived, fire, laundry) write .txt copies. Nothing writes apps/canopy-prototype/models/jeep_expedition.txt or jeep_expedition_lod.txt, which the page loads (camp/core.js:80). Their sizes match the GLBs in props/jeep/ today (359,512 bytes -> 479,352 base64), so they are in step now, by hand. bake_all.py has no jeep step, and the light bake imports whatever props/jeep/jeep_<style>.glb is on disk as the shadow caster.
findings.why: After a change to build_jeep.py three manual steps must happen in the right order (run the builder, base64 both GLBs into models/, rerun the bake). If the first is forgotten the ground shadow and prop sun map are baked against an old jeep without any warning; if the second is forgotten the page shows an old jeep under new shadows.
findings.fix: Give build_jeep.build() the same export helper the bake uses (GLB plus models/<name>.txt, per-object triangle print). Add a 'jeep' step to props/bake_all.py before 'light' that runs build_jeep.py only when the GLB is older than build_jeep.py or build_camp.py (mtime, or a small hash stamp file next to the GLB), and make the light step print a warning when it uses a GLB older than its builder. The second part edits bake_all.py, which belongs to the bakes area.

findings.title: To check: reset() reloads factory preferences, and the light bake never selects a render device afterwards

locations.snippet: def reset(): bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
build_camp.reset()
sc.cycles.device = "CPU"

findings.evidence: wm.read_factory_settings is documented as 'Load factory default startup file and preferences', so it resets the Cycles compute-device preference as well as the scene. bake_camp_lightmap.py calls build_camp.reset() at line 125 (and each lived build calls reset() before that), and after it never sets scene.cycles.device or the Cycles preferences (grep for cycles.device and compute_device in sloth: only the two CPU lines in build_camp.py:739 and build_lived.py:180). In desk-at-night every bake script sets the device explicitly after the same reset (for example blender/bake_platform.py:97-105). The GPU wrapper gpu_run.py is not in either repo, so I could not see whether it survives a factory reset (it would if it uses Cycles' process-wide --cycles-device override or wraps the bake operator; it would not if it only sets preferences and the scene device before running the script).
findings.why: If the wrapper's setting is lost at the reset, the 4K, 512-sample light bake (about 14 bake passes) runs on the CPU of the GPU machine. That would explain a costly bake better than anything in the geometry code. This is a risk to confirm, not a confirmed defect.
findings.fix: First print bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences.compute_device_type and scene.cycles.device right before the first bpy.ops.object.bake in bake_camp_lightmap.py. If it says CPU: give reset() a variant that clears the data without touching preferences (remove objects and orphan data, or bpy.ops.wm.read_homefile(use_empty=True, use_factory_startup=True)), and set the device in one shared helper after any reset, as desk-at-night does with pick_device().
findings.estimate_or_measured: Not measured and not confirmed. If confirmed the impact is high (GPU versus CPU for the whole light bake); if the wrapper already handles it, this item closes with no change.

findings.title: BUDGET decimation never triggers in the live bake and is copied inline; it would silently decimate a hand-built prop if it ever did

locations.snippet: BUDGET = {"picked": {"Table": 1400, "Seat": 500, "Lantern": 200}} ... def lean(objs, budget): ... d.decimate_type = "COLLAPSE"; d.ratio = n / tris
n = build_camp.BUDGET["picked"].get(name); t = sum(len(p.vertices) - 2 for p in o.data.polygons) ... d = o.modifiers.new("lean", "DECIMATE")

findings.evidence: The budgets were set when the objects were densified for vertex AO (commit d94cbe6: 3.1k/0.8k/344 -> 1.4k/0.5k/200). The live bake does no densify, and the props have since been trimmed: the code's own comments give the Table about 190 triangles (line 441) and the Lantern 34 (line 430); my static count for the Seat is about 164 (half log 48, top box 12, two 14-sided stumps 104). All are 3 to 7 times under budget, so the decimate block in bake_camp_lightmap.py is inert, and the Lantern is deleted before export anyway. lean() itself is only called from build() (the archive CLI); the bake script has its own copy of the same five lines. The comment at 803-804 ('after the AO bake ... the densify only gave the bake room to vary') describes the old pipeline.
findings.why: Dead in the live path, duplicated, and a trap: if someone adds detail and crosses a budget, a collapse decimate quietly rearranges a model whose triangles were placed by hand, instead of telling them.
findings.fix: In bake_camp_lightmap.py replace lines 131-135 with a check that prints each object's count and stops (or warns) when it is over BUDGET. Keep lean() only with the archive CLI (gencamp-08), or delete the bake script's copy and call build_camp.lean() if the decimate is wanted. Confirm the three counts first (see measure requests).

areas.title: Generators: lived props (build_lived.py, build_fire.py, build_laundry.py)
areas.summary: Three Blender generators (props/lived/build_lived.py 802 lines, build_fire.py 424, build_laundry.py 174) that borrow primitives from props/camp/build_camp.py. Every object they export is used by the page (checked all 18 names against apps/canopy-prototype on origin/main and the three PR branches), so there is no dead prop. Honest verdict on the "highly inefficient" fear for THIS area: the geometry code itself is cheap. By my count the three scripts make about 485 bpy.ops calls in scenes of under 100 objects (estimate: well under a second in total), and the PIL textures are drawn with ImageDraw primitives, not per-pixel loops (estimate: under half a second together). The one real cost is wood_stack(): it rebuilds a 22-log detailed stack and runs three Cycles renders on the CPU on every run, including every bake_all light step, with no cache. The larger problems are structural: (1) the page's GLBs are produced only by bake_camp_lightmap.py, which exec()s these scripts with build_camp.bake monkey-patched, lets each one reset the scene and export a GLB, then resets again, re-imports those GLBs and re-exports over them; the scripts' own AO path, --samples and the densify overrides are vestigial, and a standalone run or an aborted bake leaves the committed GLBs in a format the page does not use; (2) four copies of the same densify monkey-patch plus one dead densify(); (3) heavy copy-paste (7 image-material blocks, 14 mesh-from-bmesh blocks, 6 export calls, 5 separate n-sided tube builders); (4) constants mirrored by hand between Python, the bake script and campProps.js/activities.js, including hand-measured pixel rectangles in a rendered atlas whose content depends on a shared random stream; (5) leftovers from the kettle and the first fire in build_fire.py (3 dead functions, 7 unused materials, 4 unused imports). No PR (#14, #15, #16) touches props/ or campProps.js, so none of the fixes conflict.

findings.title: wood_stack() rebuilds the detailed log stack and runs three CPU Cycles renders on every run, with no cache

locations.snippet: def stack_logs(M): ... rows = [6, 5, 5, 4, 2]
bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
sc.cycles.device = "CPU" ... px = 900 ... _render_view(tmp % "end", ...)
stack = wood_stack(M, max(samples, 48))
("build_lived", lambda g: g["build"](32, None))

findings.evidence: Read wood_stack() fully. Each call builds 22 split logs (per log: primitive_cylinder_add, 2 apply_all, 1-2 bmesh bisect round trips, a per-vertex rough_up), sets up sun, world, camera and a wave-ring node tree, then renders 1008x576, 468x576 and 1008x468 px at max(samples, 48) samples with the device forced to CPU (line 180), composes the atlas, derives the block outline from the end render's alpha, and deletes the logs and the temp PNGs. There is no existence check, stamp or hash anywhere in the file (grep for exists/hash/stamp/mtime: none). bake_camp_lightmap.py line 83 calls build(32, None) on every light bake, so this runs each time bake_all.py runs the light step even when only a lantern moved.
findings.why: Only the 1024x1024 atlas and about 25 outline points are needed by anything downstream; the 22 logs (110 of build_lived's roughly 285 bpy.ops calls) and the three renders are pure rework when the stack has not changed. It also makes lived.glb depend on Cycles noise and on which machine and Blender version ran it (outline and atlas pixels), so a rebake for an unrelated reason can change WoodStack's geometry and with it the shared light-map packing.
findings.fix: Cache the result. Write the outline next to the atlas (props/lived/wood_stack.json: outline points, plus a stamp = hash of the source text of split_log, stack_logs, wood_stack, STACK_BOX and the sample count). At the top of wood_stack(), if wood_stack.jpg and the json exist and the stamp matches, skip stack_logs() and the renders and build the block from the saved outline; add a --rerender flag to force it. This needs stack_logs() to stop drawing from the shared rng first (genlived-02), or the chips would move when the render is skipped.
findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate, not measured: about 1.3 megapixels x 48 samples on CPU plus three scene syncs and denoise, roughly 10 to 40 s per run on the desktop and 1 to 2 minutes in a small cloud container. Small next to the 4K, 512-sample light bakes, but it is the only expensive step in this area.

findings.title: The bake drives these scripts by exec(), lets each reset the scene and export a GLB, then re-imports and re-exports the same files

locations.snippet: build_camp.bake = flat_bake ... exec(compile(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read(), path, "exec"), g)
new = import_glb(os.path.join(LIVED, f"{sname}.glb"))

def build(samples, parts_out=None):
    reset()

def build(samples=32):
    reset()

def build():
    reset()

findings.evidence: Read the whole of bake_camp_lightmap.py. Step 1 runs each build() with a fake module dict; each build() starts with reset() (read_factory_settings), builds, exports props/lived/<name>.glb and prints triangle counts. Then line 125 resets again, builds the picked set, and lines 163-184 import the three GLBs just written. At the end the same three paths are exported again with the light-map UVs. So per bake: 4 factory resets, 3 throwaway GLB exports, 3 GLB imports, and the committed GLBs are overwritten twice. The imported meshes are also what gets unwrapped (triangulated, vertices split by the exporter), not the quads and n-gons the builders made.
findings.why: The round trip exists only because build() does three jobs at once (wipe the scene, make the objects, export). It costs a few seconds per bake (estimate), hides a coupling on import details (the '.001' name stripping at line 173, the colour attribute rename at 181, un-parenting at 167), and causes the half-written state in genlived-05. Adding a fourth lived script means another exec entry, another PLACE table and another export branch.
findings.fix: Split each script's build() into make(M=None) that only creates and returns its objects in the current scene (no reset, no export), and a thin main() that does reset(), make(), bake, export for standalone previews. bake_camp_lightmap.py then imports the three modules normally, calls reset() once and make() three times, and exports once at the end. Because the light-map unwrap would then see the builders' own faces instead of the imported triangles, the atlas layout changes: one full rebake is needed and the result must be compared by eye.
findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate: 3 exports + 3 imports + 3 extra factory resets, about 3 to 8 s per light bake. The gain is mostly robustness and less code, not time.

areas.title: Across the runtime (imports, globals, helpers, PR branches)
areas.summary: Cross-cutting static analysis of the Canopy Camp runtime (23 modules in apps/canopy-prototype/camp/ + activities.js, atmosphere.js, bakedlight.js, ground.js, fur.js, camp.html, tools/camp-probe.cjs, and the 6 new modules on PR #15/#16), done with small read-only scripts (import graph, export/import table, window.__ table, URL/storage table, duplicate-body scan, unused-import scan, a diff of the pre-split script against the split modules, print-only trial merges of the PR branches). State: the 2026-11-12 split cut one script at its section headers, and the modules still behave like one script. (a) Import graph: 28 modules, 12 side-effect-only imports of which 7 just repeat a named import of the same module two lines below, 2 are not needed at all and 3 are load-bearing; one cycle (sloths.js -dynamic-> lab.js -> player.js -> sloths.js); 5 modules use top-level await (campProps, jeep, campLife, operator, main), so evaluation order is the async-module order, not the textual one. (b) Exports imported nowhere on main or any PR branch: forest.js flatCol, woodMat (never used at all), merge/jeepDist/pathDist (used only inside), jeep.js jeepTap (assigned, never called), food.js foodTris and FOOD_KINDS, deadwood.js deadwood, bakedlight.js LIGHT and GAIN (GAIN is reached through window.__lights instead), fur.js FUR_ON, terrain.js heightGrid (reached through a global). (c) 36 window.__ globals on main (41 with PR #16): 12 are the real API between modules (__camp, __jeep, __campLife, __acts, __me, __lights, __cabinLive, __laundry, __groundHeight, __lab, __labStep, __campFast), 8 are the contract with tools/camp-probe.cjs and props/shadow/export_casters.cjs, and 17 are debug hooks written and never read anywhere in the repo, none documented. (d) 18 URL options and 6 localStorage keys, documented only in scattered comments; export_casters.cjs still passes two options the page no longer reads. (e) The same small helpers exist 3 to 9 times (canvas-to-texture 5 + 6 inline, smoothstep 4 named + 16 inline, LCG random 6, segment distance 4, angle wrap 3, tent frame 5, V() 3, lam() 2, triangle counters 5). (f) Only lanterns, highlight, canister, cast, food, terrain, fur, bakedlight and the three factory files outside camp/ are side-effect free on import; everything else mutates the scene, the DOM or window while it is imported. Two real regressions surfaced: the split dropped the keyboard listeners (WASD and arrows do nothing on a computer, on main and all three PR branches), and a comment inserted mid-line in deadwood.js swallowed the dead trunk's layout line (it is missing from the bake layout). (g) PR branches: the three PRs merge pairwise without textual conflicts (print-only git merge-tree); PR #16 carries PR #15's first commit unchanged and #15 adds one commit on top in audio.js only; the new modules repeat the same patterns (5 new globals, more copies of lam/tris/tent frame, import-time scene work) and audio.js reads PR #14's acts.cook through a global, so the PRs depend on each other silently.

areas.title: Boot, input, HUD, main loop (core.js, main.js, input.js, hud.js, player.js)
areas.summary: Boot, loop and input are ten files (camp.html 67 lines, core 115, hud 13, main 140, save 16, input 149, player 78, highlight 88, linger 39, lab 119). All were read in full on origin/main (= HEAD 21d168d) and checked against PR #14, #15 and #16. The split of 2026-11-12 works and has no import cycle on main or on any of the three PR branches (checked with a small graph script; lab.js is the only module loaded with import()). The run order is still load-bearing, for three reasons: five modules use top-level await (campProps, jeep, campLife, operator, main), the seeded random stream is consumed in module order, and later modules read window.__ globals set by earlier ones. Of the eleven 'import "./prev.js"' lines, seven repeat a named import of the same module in the same file, two do nothing for the result (sky->hud, player->sloths) and two carry a real hidden dependency (forest->sky, sloths->jeep). Main themes: (1) two real regressions from the split and its follow-ups: the keyboard listeners were dropped, so WASD and arrows do nothing on a computer on main and on all three PR branches, and the fire/pot highlight is frozen at its first value; (2) main.js is both the orchestrator and the home of feature logic (night palette, flame flicker, sloth squish, effect sprites, glow uniforms, shadow poll), and core.js is a grab-bag (options, settings buttons, renderer, downloads, lights, a forest-only material); (3) runtime data crosses modules through about a dozen window.__ globals mixed with about fifteen check-only hooks, so nobody can tell which are safe to remove (window.__me is labelled a check hook but sloths.js needs it); (4) leftovers of archived choices are still in core.js (LOOK, PROPS, CABIN constants, the paint and low look tables) and in camp.html (stale header, CSS for the removed look links and friends pill); (5) start-up: three ground textures are outside the PRE table and start late, which also triggers one wasted live shadow render; base64 files are decoded with a per-character callback; compileAsync skips everything hidden at boot. Per-frame cost in these files is small (estimates only); the clearest waste is aimStep rebuilding its target list and bounding boxes each frame. URL options: 17 are read (detail, lm, jeep, lived, op, seed, time, cycle, pos, yaw, pitch, touch, campsloths, slothmat, weather, lab, fur) in 7 files with three parsing styles and no list anywhere; the bake's page call still passes ?props= and ?lm=off, which the page no longer reads. Note for the lead: PR #15 and PR #16 both add camp/audio.js (different versions) and the same #sound button on camp.html line 62, so they conflict with each other. README.md still has no row for the camp (earlier audit M8).

findings.estimate_or_measured: Estimate: 0.3 to 0.8 s of main-thread time on a desktop and 2 to 4 times that on a phone for the current decode; several times less with a plain loop. Not measured; see measure_requests.

findings.title: THREE.Clock is deprecated in three 0.186: the page logs a warning at every start

locations.snippet: const clock = new THREE.Clock(); ... const raw = clock.getDelta(), dt = Math.min(raw, 0.05);

findings.evidence: node_modules/three/src/core/Clock.js (version 0.186.1) line 61: warn('Clock: This module has been deprecated. Please use THREE.Timer instead.') with '@deprecated since r183'. tools/camp-probe.cjs collects console errors only, so the warning does not show in probe output.
findings.why: Noise in the console on every load, and the class will be removed in a later three version.
findings.fix: Use the time stamp the animation loop already passes: let last = 0; renderer.setAnimationLoop((now) => { const raw = last ? (now - last) / 1000 : 0; last = now; ... }). The first frame gets 0, as Clock.getDelta() gives now.

findings.title: The resolution safety net only goes down, and a 30 Hz display counts as slow

locations.snippet:
slow = fps < 45 ? slow + 1 : 0;
if (slow >= 2 && pr > 1) { pr = Math.max(1, pr - 0.25); renderer.setPixelRatio(pr); resize(); slow = 0; }

findings.evidence: Read the block: two seconds in a row under 45 fps lower the pixel ratio by 0.25, down to 1; nothing raises it again and nothing tells the viewer. A phone that caps the page at 30 fps (a battery-saver mode, for example) is always under 45, so Detail Medium falls from 1.75 to 1 in about 6 seconds whatever the real load is. The Detail setting then no longer says what resolution is shown; only window.__stats.pr does.
findings.why: The picture gets soft for good after one busy moment (a download finishing, a tab switch) or on any capped display, and a review screenshot can differ from the next one for no visible reason.
findings.fix: Judge by frame time against the display's own rate: measure the median frame interval in the first second as the target, lower only when the average is more than about 1.4 times that, and raise by 0.25 again (up to D.pr) after 10 good seconds. Show the current pr in the fps pill.

findings.title: Move lab: the path line reuses its first buffer, so later paths are cut short or keep an old tail

locations.snippet: if (pathLine.visible) pathLine.geometry.setFromPoints([s.o.getWorldPosition(wp).clone(), ...T.path].map((p) => V(p.x, 0.04, p.z)));

findings.evidence: three 0.186.1 BufferGeometry.setFromPoints (node_modules/three/src/core/BufferGeometry.js 596-630): when a position attribute already exists it writes only min(points.length, attribute.count) points and warns 'Buffer size too small for points data' when there are more. The line's buffer is sized by the first path shown. A later, longer path is drawn only up to that length, with a console warning every frame; a later, shorter path leaves the old path's last points in the buffer and they are still drawn, because the draw range is never set.
findings.why: The lab exists to inspect paths for flaws by eye; a wrong line there sends you looking for a path bug that is not one.
findings.fix: Give the line a fixed buffer once (for example 128 points), write the points into it without making new vectors, and call geometry.setDrawRange(0, n) each frame; if a path is longer, grow the buffer by disposing and replacing the geometry.

areas.title: Sloths (sloths.js)
areas.summary: sloths.js (1,096 lines, 91 KB, 32 lines over 200 characters) is one module doing nine jobs. Map: 14-65 building a sloth (eyeKit, hang); 66-135 per-frame life (look, wave, blink, yawn, mouth); 136-147 wild sloths; 166-287 the spots table plus the hammock-sway and laundry-cloth shader patches; 288-353 poses, slide/glide, climbs; 355-417 grid + A* wayfinding; 431-472 the window.__campLife registry (claims, movers, hosts, lend, eatGift); 473-758 fruit, eating, engine fix, cards, gifts; 759-807 walking and greeting; 809-867 s'mores, naps, z's; 869-937 cast placement, nap trips, save; 951-1057 campStep (a 17-branch phase chain); 1058-1079 debug globals and the Move-lab button; 1082-1093 sprites/fx. Lines 165-1075 are a single 910-line `if (campsloths)` closure, so nothing in it can be imported or tested, and other modules reach it through window.__campLife / window.__lab. State is kept ad hoc on the sloth object (about 40 fields, written by sloths.js, main.js, input.js, operator.js, lab.js), on s.trip (26 fields) and on spot objects (23 fields); phases are magic strings listed again in four sets. The static read found seven real bugs, the two worst being state-machine leaks: a sloth borrowed by the operator while walking to a table place leaks its claim (and deadlocks a card game), and leave() during a gift eat clip freezes the sloth for good. The hammock also loses its baked light because its material is cloned without the lnight hook. Befriending is gone but its leftovers remain (flowerCrown, COUNT, friend, perch, a second stale header). Movement code is duplicated: four copies of the hanging pose, five hand-rolled tweens, and the way into the hammock/line uses four bespoke phases while the way out uses the generic slide/glide. Runtime cost is modest per frame; the measurable waste is in sprites (every z and every word gets its own 512x128 texture, z's are drawn at opacity 0 for ever after a first nap), a 3,600-raycast first frame in pois(), and a localStorage write every 2 s. cast.js is a near-verbatim copy of a block in names-prototype.html (73 of 77 long lines); food.js is clean but its fruit table is mirrored by hand in sloths.js. The earlier audit's four P5 sloth items are done; M3 (one layout manifest) is still open here. PR #14 edits about 25 places in sloths.js and PR #16 four, so the split and most clean-ups should land after those merge.

findings.title: A sloth borrowed by the operator while walking to a table/crate place leaks the place; a card game then never ends

locations.snippet: if (s.trip.slot?.key && s.trip.slot.who === s) { s.trip.slot.who = null; life.release(s.trip.slot.key, s); }

findings.evidence: Read lend(), errand(), startCards(), startEat(), cardsStep(). lend() accepts phase "walk" (line 442). The claimed place is only put on the trip by startEat() (line 642, on arrival); while walking it lives only in the arrive closure, and leave() made a fresh s.trip (line 572). So the release at line 443 can never fire for a sloth on its way: slot.who stays s and claims keeps slot.key. errand() then skips that place for everyone (611: `!q.who && !claims.has(q.key)`), startCards() fails for good (678), and if the borrowed sloth was a card player the other one waits at line 701 for ever (g.t never advances, game stays set, it counts toward MAX_OUT). operator.js play() prefers sloths that are out walking. Not fixed in PR #14 or #16 (diffs read).
findings.why: After a few operator play sessions the table and crate places are all blocked: sloths stop eating there and never play cards again until reload; one sloth can be left sitting on the table holding cards for the rest of the session.
findings.fix: Record the destination when it is claimed: in errand() set `s.trip.slot = slot` right after each walkTo() to a claimed place (lines 601, 614), so lend()'s existing release works. In lend() also end a game the sloth belongs to (`if (game?.players.includes(s)) game.over = true`), and in cardsStep() end the game when the other player is neither walking, greeting nor eating.

findings.evidence: s.gift is only cleared by the playOnce callback held in s.once (468). Every play() sets s.once = null (309), and leave() always calls play() (lines 579, 583, 588 or via climbDown). Callers of leave() that do not check s.gift: startCards() for the mate (680, picked at 967), the camp-food listener (1061), window.__errand (1065) and __lab.leave (1068). After that s.gift.clip stays true, so campStep takes the branch at 961 every frame and never reaches the phase chain: the sloth plays the walk clip in place and the food flickers between hand and paw. lend() does guard on s.gift?.clip (442), so the case was known but not covered here. The mate search returns the first match in camp order, which is Sunny (seat) then Mango (jeep), exactly the two that eat gifts with the clip.
findings.why: Feeding Sunny on the log and having another sloth start a card game in the next 8 s (the eat clip's length) leaves Sunny stuck until reload. Estimate, not measured: a card roll happens roughly once a minute, so about one feeding of Sunny in seven.
findings.fix: Make leave() the single guard: at its top, `if (s.gift?.clip) { scene.remove(s.gift.mesh); s.gift = null; if (s.mouth) s.mouth.visible = false; }`; or refuse to leave while s.gift is set (add `!q.gift` at 967 and 1061 and in the lab/errand hooks).

findings.title: The hammock loses its baked light: its material is cloned without the lnight shader hook

locations.snippet: const mat = ham.material.clone(); mat.onBeforeCompile = (sh) => { sh.uniforms.uSway = sway; ... }; ham.material = mat;
const prevHook = mat.onBeforeCompile;   // keeps the props thread's night light (lnight)
const lnight = (mat) => { const prev = mat.onBeforeCompile; mat.lightMap = LMTEX; mat.lightMapIntensity = 0; mat.onBeforeCompile = ...

findings.evidence: campProps.js:101-102 gives every picked prop the one lnight() material; the Hammock is a single mesh named "Hammock" (props/camp/bake_camp_lightmap.py:152). In three 0.186.1 Material.copy() does not copy onBeforeCompile or customProgramCacheKey (checked node_modules/three/src/materials/Material.js: neither name appears in copy()). So the clone at line 180 keeps lightMap with intensity 0 but drops the whole baked-light shader, and the new hook at 181 does not chain the old one. The laundry cloth 50 lines below does chain it (229-231), so the omission is not intended. Nothing re-applies lnight later (grep lnight( and lightMap in camp/*.js). With ?campsloths=0 the block does not run and the hammock keeps the bake.
findings.why: The hammock is lit live only: no baked sun shadow or sky occlusion by day and none of the fire, lantern and moon light at night, unlike every prop next to it. Static finding; needs one night screenshot to confirm how visible it is.
findings.fix: Chain the hook as the cloth does (keep prev = ham.material.onBeforeCompile and call it first, and give the clone a customProgramCacheKey that includes both), or better move the sway into campProps.js next to lnight and export { sway, swing } (see sloths-32). No bake needed: the light map and UV2 are already there.

areas.title: Operator, activities, campLife (operator.js, activities.js, campLife.js)
areas.summary:
Read in full: camp/operator.js (676 lines), camp/campLife.js (64), activities.js (311), and camp/sloths.js (1,096) for the comparison; plus the PR #14/#15/#16 diffs for these files. The working tree equals origin/main for apps/. Static review only, nothing was run.

Overall: the three files work and their frame cost is small (one character, a few pooled effects), so efficiency is not the problem here. Structure is. (1) operator.js and sloths.js are two separate character engines: operator.js is a generator-coroutine state machine (DO.* + lifeLoop), sloths.js a phase/callback machine (s.trip.phase + slide/glide/move callbacks). They share only one thing by design, window.__campLife (claims, hosts, movers, A* path), which is defined inside sloths.js's `if (campsloths)` block and reached through a window global with 9 optional-chained calls. Everything else is implemented twice: aimBone (byte-for-byte), the clip cross-fade player, keep-right steering, turning, the 3-second gaze-and-wave, sleep Zs (three copies), eaten-food shrinking, random free spot, and, once PR #14 lands, a second two-bone arm solver. PR #14 adds about 200 lines to operator.js and widens every one of these gaps. (2) The operator drives sloth mixers directly (slothPose), which leaves the sloth's own clip tracking stale: by reading, a sloth he has played or napped with keeps that pose clip running at full weight afterwards (operator-01, needs a check). (3) campLife.js is leftover glue from the 2026-11-12 split: it creates ground, atmosphere and activities, but also owns the tent's walk-in collision and the stove glow, depends on statement order, still branches on archived options, and shares its name with the unrelated window.__campLife. (4) activities.js has no dead chunks: logs on the fire, the soup pot, the fruit plate, put-back and giving food are all live; the "friendship book" and "photo album" exist only in a comment (campLife.js:56). Its dead parts are small: the hidden old flame sprites it still scales each frame, the unused `blockers` option, three fallbacks that can never run. Its update() allocates nothing per frame. It is one 250-line closure fed by a 19-key options bag, and it talks to the sloths two ways at once (pokes s.nod directly and fires the window event "camp-food"). (5) Scene facts (crate, pot, tent bed and stove, log ring, table yaw, fruit plate) are copied by hand into 3 to 5 modules and build_camp.py (earlier audit M3, still open). (6) window.__op, documented as a checks-only handle, is read by audio.js in PRs #15/#16 as a production API, and that audio.js also reads acts.cook.stage, which exists only in PR #14.

Not found in these files: triangle-budget problems (props in hand are 8 to 64 tris, hit volumes are invisible), O(n^2) per-frame loops, or import cycles. Out of my files but seen on the way: main.js:63/116 keeps updating the hidden `flies` cloud each frame; weather.js is not in the "import prev" chain and, because of top-level awaits in the chain, runs before it finishes (harmless today: it uses no seeded random).

The titanic clip exists (characters/sloth_baby/sloth_rig.py:543). slothPose stops every action and starts the pose clip but leaves s.act pointing at the old (now stopped) action. On giveBack sloths.js calls play(s,"idle"): if s.act was already idle (lent while resting or greeting) it returns early, so idle never restarts and titanic plays on alone; otherwise it cross-fades from the stale stopped action to idle and the pose clip stays active at weight 1 next to it. Nothing later stops the pose clip, so it keeps blending about 50/50 with walk, cling and so on until the operator next picks that sloth up. Same for "curl" after a nap together. Same code on PR #14. Not run: reasoning from three.js AnimationAction semantics only.

findings.fix: Smallest: in slothPose, after a.reset().play(), set `s.act = a; s.once = null;` so sloths.js cross-fades from the pose clip. Cleaner: add `pose(s, clip, fade)` to the life object in sloths.js that calls its own play(), and have operator.js call life().pose instead of touching s.mixer.

findings.title: Sleep loop does not do what its comment says ("up a little after the light")

locations.snippet: for (let t = 0, T = R(40, 80); (night() ? true : t < T);) { ... if (night() && t > 600) t = 0; if (!night() && op.wasNight && t > 8) break;

findings.evidence: Read the loop. t counts seconds asleep, not seconds since dawn. At dawn either t >= T (the loop condition ends it the same frame) or t > 8 (the break ends it the same frame). The 8 s grace only happens if `t = 0` at 600 s happened less than 8 s before dawn. The `t > 600` reset has no other purpose.

findings.fix: Track dawn explicitly: `let dawn = 0; ... if (!night() && op.wasNight) dawn = 1e-3; if (dawn) { dawn += dt; if (dawn > 8) break; }` and drop the t > 600 reset and the `night() ? true :` trick (`while (night() || t < T || dawn)`).

areas.title: World (forest.js, sky.js, terrain.js, ground.js, atmosphere.js, deadwood.js)
areas.summary:
The world layer is seven files (forest.js 378 lines, sky.js 131, terrain.js 52, deadwood.js 129, weather.js 51, ground.js 487, atmosphere.js 272), all read line by line. None of the open PRs #14, #15 or #16 changes any of them; only main.js (#15, #16) and the new audio.js are touched near this area.

Structure: sky.js paints the backdrop and domes. forest.js owns the whole layout (clearing radius, path, glade, jeep spot and track) and also grows the trees, leaves and ferns. terrain.js is a clean, import-free height function fed by forest.js through initTerrain. ground.js and atmosphere.js are dependency-injected factories called once from campLife.js. weather.js is small and self-contained.

Main themes:
- **Two real bugs with visible or baked consequences.** A swallowed line in deadwood.js keeps the dead trunk out of the shadow bake, the triangle report and the ground seating. The bowl rim has an 8.7 cm step along the -x axis.
- **The three looks are unreachable.** LOOK is the constant "moss" on main and all three PR branches, yet about 45 paint/low/flat branches remain across forest.js, sky.js, ground.js and core.js. core.js:8-10 says they are dead "until the forest moves to its own module", which has happened. The detail levels (low, medium, high) are all still reachable.
- **Dead leftovers from decided options.** Jeep and door ground-light samplers in the ground shader, the shade disc bookkeeping, two hidden floor discs kept only for their textures, the old firefly cloud in main.js, the kettle spout steam, and unused helpers and exports in forest.js.
- **Order coupling through the one seeded stream.** forest.js draws texture noise and detail-dependent leaf counts from the layout stream, so the wild sloths' hang spots, sun shafts and motes differ per detail level. Any clean-up in forest.js must keep the exact draw sequence, or the trunks, mounds and height grid move and the baked maps no longer match.
- **Duplication.** Four canvasTex copies, four smoothstep copies, eight copies of the same LCG, three polyline-distance loops, two ribbon builders, three leaf-instancing loops, and hand-mirrored constants (sun direction, RR, radius 30, tent bounds).
- **Start-up cost.** The backdrop makes about 72,600 canvas fill calls (counted with a mock 2D context; the time is not measured). The ground maps bypass PRE, so they start late and can race the loading card.

Per-frame cost in these files is small. The ground fragment shader is the only place with meaningful GPU waste.

Side note for the bake area: props/shadow/export_casters.cjs still passes `?props=` and `lm=off`, which the page no longer reads, so the export run loads the 2K light maps.

Commit fac63a0 ("no worn dirt or path to the fallen log...") added the comment in front of them. Parsed the committed props/shadow/layout_picked.json: `deadwood` holds FallenLog and Stump only. The line is identical on origin/main and all three PR branches. bake_camp_lightmap.py:249 has a DeadTrunk occluder branch that therefore never runs. ground.js casters() also excludes the merged Deadwood mesh (bb.max.y 4.6 > 4.5), so the live fallback casts nothing for it either.

findings.title: Bowl rim height has an 8.7 cm step along the -x axis (atan2 seam in the rim noise)

locations.snippet: const k = vnoise(Math.atan2(z, x) * 1.6 + 11, 0.5); const bowl = (0.22 + 0.3 * k) * ss(RC - 0.8, RC + 2.2, r);

findings.evidence: The rim noise is sampled on the angle, which jumps from +pi to -pi on the -x axis. Evaluated the file's own hash and vnoise in node: k(+pi) = 0.2416, k(-pi) = 0.5317, so rim height is 0.292 m against 0.380 m, a 0.087 m step. The track heads toward -z and the glade is at +1.67 rad, so `open` is 1 on the -x axis and the step is fully present from r = 11.2 m out to FAR = 30.
findings.why: The ground mesh (ground.js ringGround, 80 segments) turns the step into a straight radial crease about 19 m long through the forest floor. The same function feeds the bake's height grid (heightGrid to layout_picked.json), so the crease is baked too.
findings.fix: Make the rim noise periodic, e.g. `vnoise(Math.cos(a) * 1.3 + 11, Math.sin(a) * 1.3 + 5)` with a = atan2(z, x). This changes rim heights everywhere by a few centimetres, so the height grid must be re-exported and the ground maps rebaked. Bundle it with the next planned bake.

areas.title: Repo hygiene (git, Pages, CI, README, tools)
areas.summary: Repo hygiene, static review of origin/main (21d168d) plus the three PR branches. The tracked tree is 96.7 MB in 202 files; apps/canopy-prototype is 56.8 MB of it (59%) and the 4K light maps alone are 34.8 MB. The .git pack is 317 MB, and 82% of all blob bytes in history are light-map PNGs (the 4K maps alone 193 MB): every rebake adds about 53 MB that can never be removed without a history rewrite. The Pages workflow copies the whole folder, so it publishes the 4K maps the code calls "local only", three old prototype pages, and serves the old Hide and Seek prototype at the folder URL. No file under apps/canopy-prototype/models is strictly unreferenced (all are reachable through template strings in camp/core.js and camp/campLife.js), but camp_shadow_picked_none.png is a stale orphan from a retired bake script. Byte-identical duplicates: sloth.txt x5, fur.js x4, ponytail.txt x2; fur.js exists in three diverged variants while the README says it is shared. Every GLB that reaches a page is stored twice (binary + base64 .txt), including the archives, where both copies sit in the same folder (7.9 MB of derivable .txt). There is no .gitattributes, so git grep and git diff treat megabyte base64 lines as text. package-lock.json is ignored (Playwright ^1.49 resolves to 1.65.0 today), there is no requirements file or Blender version pin, package.json has one script, and there is no lint, test or CI check: the only workflow deploys on push with nothing in front of it. README.md and CLAUDE.md do not mention Canopy Camp, props/, the bake pipeline, tools/ or GitHub Pages at all, although that is where nearly all current work happens; the rules this review was given (bakes only on the GPU thread, import order matters, module owners, trip hooks) are written nowhere in the repo. Several comments point at things that no longer exist (camp.html header, the otpcew integration branch, props/shadow/bake_ground_shadow.py, JEEPS in camp.html). Notes for other areas: a static import/export check I ran (28 modules, 264 named imports, 0 broken) lists 14 exports nobody imports on main or any PR branch (deadwood.js:deadwood, food.js:foodTris and FOOD_KINDS, forest.js:flatCol, jeepDist, merge, pathDist, woodMat, jeep.js:jeepTap, lab.js:toggle, terrain.js:heightGrid, bakedlight.js:LIGHT and GAIN, fur.js:FUR_ON); some are reached through window.__ globals instead. PR #16 already contains PR #15's first commit (484de6d), and the two merge cleanly. Branch claude/project-thread-n6c974 (not one of the three listed PRs) adds tools/camp-replay.cjs and a package.json script, so package.json edits should be coordinated with it.

findings.evidence: .github/ holds only pages.yml; it has no pull_request trigger and its build job only copies files. tools/camp-probe.cjs already collects page errors, console errors and 4xx responses and waits for window.__ready, but exits 0 whatever it finds. The camp is 28 ES modules chained by side-effect imports (import "./prev.js") edited by several threads at once, with three open PRs. I ran two read-only checks on main: node --check on all 28 modules (clean) and a 30-line import/export resolver (264 named imports, 0 broken) in under a second; scratch script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/5e5ccd13-efc0-592c-83dc-1d72c08220b1/scratchpad/agents/hygiene/imports.cjs.

findings.title: No .gitattributes: megabyte base64 lines are treated as text by git grep, git diff and PR views
findings.evidence: ls .gitattributes: missing. git ls-files --eol shows 36 files as 'i/none' text: 30 base64 .txt files (13.9 MB) plus 5 .ktx2.txt (7.1 MB) and props/shadow/layout_picked.json (96,816 B, one line). During this review 'git grep 4k -- props' matched inside props/camp/archive/camp_jungle.txt, camp_picked.txt, camp_rustic.txt, camp_storybook.txt and both archived jeep .txt files, and 'git grep 8765' matched inside camp_lm_2k.ktx2.txt.
findings.why: Every agent has to remember 'never grep the models' because git does not know they are data. One forgotten path filter dumps megabytes into a session. PR diffs of a rebake show unreadable megaline changes. With bakes committed from Windows, eol handling is also left to each machine's autocrlf setting.
findings.fix: Add .gitattributes: 'apps/**/models/*.txt binary', 'stickers/renderer/models/*.txt binary', 'props/**/archive/*.txt binary', 'props/shadow/layout_picked.json -diff', '*.glb binary', '*.ktx2 binary', and 'linguist-generated' on the same patterns. Git then prints 'Binary file matches' and skips them in diffs.

findings.title: package-lock.json is ignored and http-server comes from npx: installs are not reproducible

locations.snippet: package-lock.json
"playwright": "^1.49.0"
// the repo's own playwright may want a browser build that isn't installed; fall back to the preinstalled Chromium

findings.evidence: The untracked lock in this checkout resolves playwright ^1.49.0 to 1.65.0. camp-probe.cjs carries a workaround for exactly that drift (fallback executablePath), export_casters.cjs has a different one (CHROME env), and stk_run.cjs, stk_anim.cjs and shot.cjs have none. 'npm run serve' calls npx http-server, which is not in devDependencies, so it is fetched unpinned at run time.
